b1prime_refreeze.change_class: class-1 (selection-relevant instrument change) — re-freeze + full A/Rsem/C re-run of both backends
b1prime_refreeze.authority: Review by two practising power-systems engineers recorded in E2_backend_transfer.md §8 (2026-07-26): D1 diagnosis and B1 repair directive
b1prime_refreeze.defect_repaired: E2 scenarios are self-built networks whose complete build existed ONLY inside reference_code, while the prompt carried only the NL request — which nonetheless referred to internal element names ('ldb'/'cap1'/'l34'). Ground truth was therefore unreachable in principle: 355/360 condition-C generations invented a substitute network and accuracy sat on a 1.1–5.6% floor (D1 diagnosis; matcher-layer correction rescued 0/202, so the defect is in bench construction, not measurement).
b1prime_refreeze.repair: Each self-built item gained a 'network_setup_code' field: the library import plus the network-construction block lifted VERBATIM out of its own reference_code. The prompt renderer (utils.render_benchmark_task_text) emits '<pointer clause><frozen request>' followed by the fenced setup block, so the task is self-contained — aligning these items with the pandapower main line, whose prompts name a loadable standard case.

items_made_self_contained.pypsa: 89/90 (e2pypsa_fb4adf622717 untouched: PyPSA ac-dc-meshed example is a loadable standard network already named in the query)

invariants_held.demand_export_rationale: The pointer clause is emitted by the renderer rather than stored in the query precisely so the demand export stays valid: storing it shifted the zero-shot TF-IDF top-10 candidate set on ~100% of items (mean Jaccard 0.56 opendss / 0.68 pypsa), which would have steered condition C's injection with boilerplate tokens AND desynchronised C (frozen export) from Rsem (runtime SBERT over the query). With the clause in the renderer, every selector input — demand export, SBERT retrieval, query-derived layer need — is byte-identical to B2.

verification.self_sufficiency: For every migrated item, network_setup_code + the reference program's post-build tail was executed in an isolated subprocess and had to reproduce ground_truth: opendss 90/90, pypsa 89/89. This is a forward proof that what the prompt now HANDS the model suffices to reach GT.
verification.prompt_assembly: 5 sampled items per backend (one per task family) built through the production paths (condition A via build_benchmark_prompt(render_benchmark_task_text), condition C via ProactiveInjector.build_messages): setup block present in both arms, backend import present, every element name referenced by the request resolvable in the setup code (the single exception is 'lnew' in e2pypsa_f0dca0731238, the line the task asks to ADD). Corpus-wide: 90/90 and 89/90 rendered prompts carry the block.
verification.answer_leak: None — the setup code is the pre-modification network. D3 items keep their un-named semantic targets ('the weakest node'), which the model must still resolve from the given network; GT still requires solving.

system_prompt_library_slot.defect_found_during_verification: Condition A built its system prompt from a hard-coded 'You are a Power System Python code generator for the pandapower library', while conditions B/C/X/R/Rsem build theirs from the backend's LibrarySpec. On the E2 backends this told the bare baseline to answer in the WRONG library: 360/360 condition-A generations imported pandapower and 0/360 imported the backend under test, versus 0/360 pandapower in the injected arms.
system_prompt_library_slot.consequence: The B2-run A arm is a wrong-library artifact, so the surviving D1 signal 'exec direction C>A in 4/4 cells' is confounded by the system prompt rather than attributable to injection.
system_prompt_library_slot.repair: utils.SYSTEM_PROMPT_BENCHMARK / SYSTEM_PROMPT_FIX are now templates filled from BENCHMARK_LIBRARY (utils.benchmark_library_name()). Unset — every pandapower run — resolves to 'pandapower' and the prompts are byte-identical to before. The E2 submit scripts set BENCHMARK_LIBRARY=opendssdirect / pypsa, which restores parity with the main line, where the baseline IS told its library.
system_prompt_library_slot.reversibility: policy-reversible without code changes: drop the env var from the submit scripts to restore the previous behaviour. Reviewed by two practising power-systems engineers; this is a second instrument change inside the same re-freeze, made because re-running with a knowingly wrong-library baseline would have burned the re-run.
